**r7 review 7 (W-lead dressing path, D-F2; H.23(l)).** The **W-lead dressing path** replaces the straight segment from each CR hole to the tab X top edge. Every W lead leaves its CR joint inside the A.3 RTV bead and joins the **trunk**, which runs +y on the footprint along x 25.80. W3 runs up x 24.40 from its hole and pairs with W4 at y 57.00; W6/W7 join at y 59.20 and W1/W2 at y 62.60. The trunk passes onto tab Y and turns +x at y 69.60, on the -y side of the FT2 fill-hole disc. It rises to y 71.10 past the U101 courtyard and the +x pocket, and to y 71.75 past the tap pads. It leaves the CR at the tab Y +x edge (x 37.56) and reaches the MB tie base A1 at (60.50, 73.50) without crossing tab X.

From A1 the **west group** (W1, W2, W6, W7) runs to (58.00, 76.00) and straight up x 58.00 to the MB +y edge. The **east group** (W3, W4, W5) runs up x 61.00 to (61.00, 85.50), clear of D-FC-EN and C-D1, and then to the MB tie base A2 at (71.50, 88.00). It crosses the MB +y edge within 30 mm of A2. W5 rises at J101 and folds once toward -x at >= 8 mm above the CR top to (28.70, 46.83). It runs +y over the footprint interior to (28.70, 73.10), then +x at y 73.10. It steps to y 73.80 over x 42.00-44.50, clear of the tap pads, and stays at its fold height until A1. From A1 it lies flat on the MB with the east group.

The **dressing rule** keeps every W lead >= 2 mm in plan from the pin-10 joint, the IN strip (C102a/b/c, R102, D107), the U101 courtyard and the +x pocket. The same 2 mm applies to every 1x10 and 1x12 post tip and every tap pad, and no W lead lies over the tab X tap field. The designed path meets the rule at the jacket edge: minimum 2.02 mm (W5), 2.08 mm (W3) and 2.09 mm for the other leads. It keeps 2.03 mm from the tap-field courtyard. The jacket envelopes are ASSUMPTIONS (half-width 2.37 mm for the trunk, 1.73 mm for the west group, 2.00 mm for the east group and the W3/W4 pair, 1.00 mm for one 18 AWG lead; TODO(measure: MS2/MS7)). The MB rework points C-D2 with R171, D-FC-EN with its EN bodge resistor, and C-D1 keep >= 1.5 mm: 4.21 mm, and 2.03 mm for W5.

W5 has two exceptions to the 2 mm rule. Over the J101 region (x 37.00-40.75) the ribbon edge lies 0.775 mm in plan from C102b, because A.8 sets the J101 region 0.50 mm below the IN strip. There the ribbon is >= 8 mm above the CR top, held by the spacer bead S1. On tab Y the ribbon overlaps the L-FC body by 0.68 mm in plan, >= 12.3 mm above the MB (L-FC body height TODO(verify: L-FC datasheet)). Both exceptions wait for an operator ruling (J.2 item 62). W5 also passes over the FT2 fill hole at its fold height, so a re-bed of FT2 first lifts W5 from S2 and S3.

The 10 mm switched-conductor clearance of the r7 rev-2 routes cannot be met on the CR. The designed path keeps 3.39 mm from the L-FC body, and W5 overlaps it in plan by 0.68 mm. The L-FC body lies 0.862 mm past the tab Y +y edge, and the 2 mm dressing rule closes every other exit from the footprint. A raster search over every plan path that keeps the 2 mm rule gives at best 5.12 mm for the trunk bundle and 9.34 mm for a single lead. From A1 on, every lead keeps 10.38-13.01 mm. The 10 mm figure has no stated pickup basis, so its acceptance on the CR is an open operator ruling (J.2 item 62).

The **anchor rule** replaces the r5 chassis-tie rule: the unsupported lead length between two anchors is <= 30 mm, measured along the lead. The anchors are the A.3 joint beads, two CR RTV beads, three W5 spacer beads and two MB tie bases:

- RTV beads (3.0 x 3.0 mm footprint, ASSUMPTION): **B1** at (25.80, 64.50) and **B3** at (35.00, 70.80);
- W5 **spacer beads**, each an RTV bead onto an insulating spacer on the CR that holds the ribbon at its fold height: **S1** at (36.00, 46.83), **S2** at (28.70, 55.00) and **S3** at (35.00, 73.10), which merges with B3 into one spot;
- **tie base A1**, 6 x 6 mm, centred at (60.50, 73.50) +- 1.5 mm, and **tie base A2**, 10 x 10 mm, centred at (71.50, 88.00) +- 1.5 mm, each bonded on the MB solder mask (sizes ASSUMPTION, TODO(verify: adhesive tie-base datasheet)).

The longest span between anchors is 25.8 mm (B3 to A1). Each tie-base zone (the base +- 1.5 mm) lies on the MB outside the CR shadow, clear of every MB part box (A1 0.51 mm from SNS-FC, A2 1.72 mm from CSNS-FC) and of every non-GND via. Under A1 the VBUS-FC layer-1 copper lies under solder mask; under A2 there is only the GND pour. The S1 and S2 footprints are ASSUMPTIONS that reach 0.50 mm into the J101 region and 0.25 mm from the W6/W7 pads; the T-A-06 dry fit places them clear of both. The chassis tie past the MB +y edge is an extra anchor with no distance limit, so the run from the last tie base to the chassis tie is exempt from the 30 mm rule. That run also meets the rule when the chassis tie sits within 4.4 mm (west group), 18.4 mm (W3/W4) or 19.4 mm (W5) past the MB +y edge; MS2 records the position.

A **polyimide strip** (0.125 mm film with silicone adhesive, cut from the polyimide sheet stock) lies on the MB under the leads, from the tab Y +x edge to the MB +y edge. It follows the lead path within x 36.06-65.28, y 65.30-92.80 (lead envelope + 2.0 mm, via pad rims included) and stops at each tie-base footprint, so each base bonds to the MB solder mask. It covers CSNS-FC, MDAC-FC, OP-FC, ROP1-FC and SNS-FC where the leads cross them. It also covers nine untented non-GND vias (H.23(c2)): 3V3 (43.43, 71.63), (46.23, 71.63) and (61.79, 79.18); CS-MDAC-FC (49.99, 72.60); FC-CURR (51.16, 74.67), (58.93, 83.57) and (60.71, 90.42); MOSI (53.46, 73.29); and SCK (53.85, 72.14). It further covers 3V3 (51.10, 69.13) and MISO (54.00, 69.60), which W5 would cross if it touched down before A1. The CR-top tips of pins 7-10 (pin 10 VCHG-IN, 0.940 mm proud, H.23(j)) get a cured dome of the BOM RTV or a Kapton patch before any lead is dressed (PM4 (6), T-F-12).

**r7 review 7 (lengths, D-F2 and D-F3; H.23(l)).** The following table gives the routes on the dressing path and the build length or maximum of each lead.

| Lead | Reference placement: route / build length or maximum (mm) | Corridor fallback (i): route / build length or maximum (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | 199.5 / fixed **0.30 m +- 10 mm** (slack 100.5) | 225.5 / fixed **0.30 m +- 10 mm** (slack 74.5) |
| W2 | 202.2 / fixed **0.30 m +- 10 mm** (slack 97.8) | 228.2 / fixed **0.30 m +- 10 mm** (slack 71.8) |
| W3 | 156.6 / **200** | 150.8 / **190** |
| W4 | 156.3 / **200** | 151.0 / **190** |
| W6 | 106.8 / **140** | 119.2 / **150** |
| W7 SCL | 123.7 / **160** | 150.7 / **190** |

| W5 (fixed 304.8 mm factory cable) | 202.7 / minimum fit **222.7** (slack 82.1) | 184.6 / minimum fit **204.6** (slack 100.2) |

W1 and W2 keep a fixed build length of 0.30 m +- 10 mm at every placement (D-F3). A shorter W1/W2 lowers the lead inductance and raises the hard-short IN-side spike at U101 (H.5). Cut to the 199.5 mm route, W1 gives 34.4 V; cut to the r7 rev-2 route of 181.6 mm, it gives 34.9 V, 1.1 V below D107 VBR(min) 36 V. At 290-300 mm the spike stays at 32.8-32.9 V, so the r3-r6 basis of H.5, H.19 and T-C-04 holds. The W1/W2 slack is a service loop anchored on the EVM plate. W3/W4, W6 and W7 keep the 0.30 m cap until MS2 and then take their route maxima; corridor fallbacks (ii) and (iii) still fail.

The route of W5 is a minimum-fit check, not a build maximum: route + a 20 mm 3-D allowance for the J101 rise and fold and the J201 drop (ASSUMPTION, T-A-06). The 0.30 m factory cable leaves 82.1 mm of slack at the reference placement and 100.2 mm in fallback (i). The slack is a service loop anchored on the EVM plate beside the EIB, and no slack lies over the CR. At 310 mm each, the W1/W2 pair has 20.65 mOhm (37.2 mV and 66.9 mW at 1.80 A), 0.66 mOhm above the H.11 figure at 0.30 m. At the 200 mm route maxima the W3/W4 pair has 8.38 mOhm (26.0 mV and 80.5 mW at 3.10 A; 26.9 mV and 86.3 mW at 3.21 A).

The USB corridor width is the Teensy 4.1 receptacle silkscreen outline from the MB `.brd`, not the plug overmold. The overmold width, thickness and length, the boot width and the bend direction are TODO(measure: MS2). W3/W4 use the 4.97 mm channel between the EVM right edge (x 88.50) and the corridor. W5 is routed around the channel over the EVM plate, so W3/W4 and W5 do not share it. The channel criterion is a clear width over y 118.04-138.73, between the EVM right edge with any clamp body and the measured plug envelope, of >= the measured W3/W4 pair OD + 1.0 mm (MS2). When it fails, corridor fallback (i) applies (A.7).
